purpose: A hand-written, fail-closed record of every canonical feature this project is measured against, with its real status and the evidence behind it. A feature that is absent is recorded as absent with a reason; it is never left out, because a row that does not exist is a gap nobody decided on.

verdicts.present: Shipped, with implementation, documentation and a focused test named below.
verdicts.partial: Some of it ships. What is missing is stated in `missing`.
verdicts.absent: Not built. The reason is stated in `reason`, and it is a known gap rather than an oversight.
verdicts.not-applicable: Cannot apply to this project, with the exact reason. Never used for convenience.

features.name: English, Cantonese and bilingual modes
features.note: Verified across 162 screens in all three modes with no clipped text.

features.name: Per-language funny-level sliders, 1 to 5
Spoken narrator with language choice
features.note: The per-language voice picker this row once recorded as absent has shipped all along. components/narrator-settings.tsx renders one radiogroup per narrated language, filtered by supportsNarratorLanguage, with an automatic option, a network-backed warning, and an honest state when a chosen voice is not installed that keeps the choice rather than resetting it. Rate and pitch are there too. They sit inside a collapsed details element, which is the likeliest reason an audit concluded they did not exist. resolveNarratorVoice, missingSelection and networkBacked are covered by tests/narrator.test.mjs.

features.name: Super-advanced regex builder beside every search
features.missing: Not present on every dropdown and right-click menu, which the contract requires without exemption for short menus.

features.name: Non-blocking notifications with a reviewable centre
features.note: A stacking corner surface with per-severity dismissal and a reviewable centre. Warnings, errors and progress do not leave on their own; information and success do. Retries supersede rather than stack. The centre searches with the shared matcher and its regex builder, filters by kind and day, multi-selects, previews what will change against what is selected, and exports in eleven formats. Driven in the built artifact.

features.name: Local version history for user-owned records
features.missing: Disruption history is recorded and browsable; there is no Git-backed per-record history with diff, restore and retention.

features.name: Export in every format that can carry the data
features.missing: Eleven formats now exist and state what each cannot carry before writing: JSON, JSON Lines, CSV, TSV, YAML, TOML, XML, Markdown, HTML, SQL and JSON Schema. The notification centre offers all of them honouring its filter. The journey export still writes only JSON and the disruption history only NDJSON; neither has been moved onto the shared writers yet.

features.name: Keyboard operation, names, contrast, targets, reduced motion
features.note: 162 screens: 0 undersized targets, 0 unnamed controls. Contrast enforced by the theme generator at 4.5:1.

features.name: Narrow widths and display scales without clipping
features.note: 320, 390 and 1440 px at 100, 150 and 200 per cent: no horizontal overflow.

features.name: Material Design 3 tokens, type, shape, elevation, state, motion
Browser-style tabs with overflow, pinning, grouping and four searches
features.reason: Navigation is a Material rail and bar with four destinations and a More dialog. The tab contract, including pinning, grouping and the four tab searches, is not built.

features.name: Ctrl+Shift+F command palette that teleports to the exact element
features.missing: Built, wired and driven in the built artifact: fifteen checks through the debugging protocol against the served document cover the shortcut, focus, the row count, a real control rendered inline, a search, a control that changes the real theme, a teleport that lands the focus on the exact element, and Escape. Two captures at 1440 in both themes, bound to their commit. It is partial rather than present for two reasons. A choice with more than four options keeps its full control on the settings surface, because a long dropdown inside a palette row would need its own search and regex builder to meet this project own contract for a dropdown. And it is absent from the interaction ledger, which drives the deployed site and cannot be re-recorded until this work is deployed.

features.name: Per-element appearance editor with Word-depth typography and an infinite colour picker
features.reason: Not built. Appearance is theme and language only.

features.name: Per-element toy locks with six credential policies, and Support Tickets
features.reason: Not built. Nothing here holds anything a person would want to put a speed bump in front of: no account, no saved credential, no private record beyond a locally stored trip.

features.name: The unlock ladder on a surface that can lock a visitor out
features.reason: Nothing here authenticates a visitor or locks one out. There is no account, no sign-in and no lockout, so there is no wait for a ladder to shorten. It becomes applicable the moment any surface can refuse entry.

features.name: Focus, low stimulation, time awareness, one thing at a time, momentum
features.reason: Not built. This is a genuine gap: a journey planner is exactly the kind of surface where time awareness and one-thing-at-a-time would help, so the absence is an omission rather than a poor fit.

features.name: Universal renamable School mode with a shared unlock credential
features.reason: Not built. It depends on a shared application-data record and a credential store that a browser-only surface does not have, so shipping it would need a different persistence story first.

features.name: Local personal-vocabulary JSON upload control
features.reason: Not built. No control is shown, and no built-in mappings ship, so the surface renders its original wording.

features.name: Multi-select and bulk actions on every list
features.missing: Built and shipped on the notification centre: multi-select, a select-all that states whether it means this page or every match, inverse selection, a preview separating what is selected from what will change with the reason for each skip, and a destructive action behind the two-key gate. The selection module is general, but the saved trips, the destination list, the vehicle tracker and the disruption history do not use it yet.

features.name: In-app changelog with a date picker and commit links
features.reason: Not built in the app. CHANGELOG.md and the release notes carry the record.

features.name: Ten per cent chance of a dim sum dish at startup
features.reason: Release code names and their photos ship. The in-app startup surprise is not built.

features.name: Logo presets and a bounded local custom upload
features.reason: Not built. The shipped mark is fixed.

features.name: Categorised local file converter with bundled adapters
features.reason: Not built. Nothing in this project produces or accepts a file a person would convert; its exports are text and its inputs are published feeds.

features.name: Local Ollama suite manager
features.reason: Not built. There is no model, no inference and no local runtime anywhere in this project, so there is nothing for a suite manager to manage.

features.name: Browser-extension download start, progress and completion surfaces
features.reason: This project ships no browser extension and no download capture path, so there is no handoff for those surfaces to receive.

features.name: Two-key super confirmation before a destructive action
features.note: This row was not-applicable because nothing here performed an irreversible action. Forgetting a notification is one, so the gate is built: two keys turned independently, then a full slider sweep, with an emergency exit that is never disabled and a re-entry guard in the state machine rather than only on the button. Verified in a browser that one key leaves the slider inert and a 90 per cent drag still refuses.

features.name: A real product embed graphic when a link is shared
features.missing: Open Graph tags are emitted, but there is no committed social-preview image at the repository root and nothing verifies that the served og:image is absolute and fetchable without credentials.

features.name: Scheduled language and appearance, with external sources
features.reason: Not built. Journey scheduling is a routing input, not a settings schedule.

features.name: Open an export in an external editor
features.reason: A browser cannot launch a local editor, and this project ships no desktop application to do it from.

features.name: Pickers and real defaults rather than empty boxes
features.note: Places, agencies, routes and race endpoints all come from published data through pickers.

features.name: A documentation site carrying the same contracts
features.reason: There is no published documentation site. The docs live in the repository.
